analytic.title: Work-in-Progress: Non-Preemptive Scheduling of Periodic Tasks with Data Dependency upon Heterogeneous Multiprocessor Platforms

div.p: Heterogeneous multiprocessor platforms have been widely adopted as an efficient approach to providing high instruction throughput while keeping power and complexity under control. Although this approach can achieve improved performance for large-scale real-time systems, it results in a complex task scheduling problem. All tasks should be scheduled according to a proper strategy such that their deadlines will be met even in the worst case situations. In this work, we study the non-preemptive scheduling problem of periodic tasks with data dependency upon heterogeneous multiprocessor platforms. We first analyze the space, time and precedence constraints of tasks, and propose an exact formulation to determine the schedulability of tasks. Then, inspired from the Heterogeneous Earliest Finish Time (HEFT) algorithm, we present a list-based scheduling heuristic to schedule the jobs generated by the periodic tasks and minimize the jobs' finish time. The proposed approach is efficient and can help in guiding the design of heterogeneous multiprocessor systems.

div.head: I. INTRODUCTION
div.p: With the rapid development of electrical and computer engineering, heterogeneous multiprocessor platforms have been widely adopted in various industrial systems to provide high processing capability while keeping power and complexity under control [9]. Especially in large-scale embedded systems, there is an increasing trend towards implementing multiple functionalities upon heterogeneous platforms comprised of different types of processing units, such as CPUs, DSP chips, graphics co-processors, hardware accelerators, etc., and each type of processing units is specialized to perform a different function most efficiently [2]. Heterogeneous multiprocessor platforms adapt to different types of computing requirements, and dramatically improve performance and conserve energy with respect to homogeneous ones [12]. Experiences on the Alpha processors show that the heterogeneous multiprocessor architecture, by dynamically choosing the most appropriate processor to execute the applications, can dramatically reduce the average power consumption by 39% [8].

Although heterogeneous multiprocessor platforms provide notable benefits to real-time systems, they give rise to a challenging task scheduling problem. Typically in systems composed of periodic tasks with data dependency, all tasks should be scheduled according to a proper strategy such that all of space, time and precedence constraints would be satisfied even in the worst case situations [5]. Since each periodic task consists an infinite number of jobs that are periodically activated [1], designers have to provide a guarantee that all tasks' jobs can be executed on heterogeneous processors and the executions with precedence constraints can be completed before their deadlines [4]. The scheduling problem upon heterogeneous multiprocessor platforms is one of the most studied problems in the real-time systems community, and has been proven to be NP-Hard in the strong sense [2].

Periodic tasks with data dependency are frequently adopted in practical real-time applications such as signal processing and process control when continual sampling, transferring and processing of data are accurately required and considered [6]. The range of application domains where one error may lead to a catastrophic consequence makes the scheduling of these systems very challenging and important. Faced with this difficult situation, system designers inevitably tend to rely on decision-making tools to determine whether all tasks are schedulable upon a heterogeneous multiprocessor platform and to achieve a proper time and processor allocation for each task.

In this work, we address the non-preemptive scheduling problem of periodic tasks with data dependency upon heterogeneous multiprocessor platforms. The main objective of our research is to solve two aspects in a real-time system:
1. How to determine whether all periodic tasks with data dependency are schedulable upon a heterogeneous multiprocessor platform?
2. If the periodic tasks with data dependency are schedulable, how to schedule the tasks such that all time and precedence constraints would be satisfied?

The non-preemptive scheduling problems of periodic tasks with data dependency are very challenging. Not only does the non-preemptive aspect add computational complexity on these problems [3], but also the data dependency constraints make them more difficult to derive the schedulability conditions. In this work, we first analyze the space, time and precedence constraints of tasks and propose an exact formulation to determine whether all tasks are schedulable. Then we present a list-based scheduling algorithm to assign optimal offsets and assignments to jobs generated by the periodic tasks and to minimize the jobs' finish time.

div.head: II. SYSTEM MODEL A. Task and Job Model
div.p: In this work, we consider a real-time system constituted of m heterogeneous processors on which n periodic tasks are scheduled. A directed acyclic graph G(T, E) is used to describe the dependency of tasks, where T = {τ 1 , τ 2 , ..., τ n } is a set of periodic tasks represented by vertices and E = {e i,j | τ i , τ j ∈ T } is the set of directed edges denoting data dependency. Each edge e i,j indicates that task τ j can start to run only after all data from τ i has been received. An example of a directed acyclic graph depicting periodic tasks with data dependency is given in Fig. 1. Each edge e i,j has an associated data transfer size data i,j , which denotes the amount of data produced by τ i that needs to be transmitted to τ j . τ i is called as the predecessor of τ j , and τ j is the successor of τ i . We use P red(τ i ) and Succ(τ i ) to denote all predecessors and successors of τ i , i.e., P red
div.formula: (τ i ) = {τ x | ∀x, e x,i ∈ E}, Succ(τ i ) = {τ x | ∀x, e i,x ∈ E}.
div.p: A task τ i is characterized by a quadruple τ i = r 1 i , c i , d i , p i where r 1 i is the release time of the first job of τ i , c i is the computation workload quantified in unit of machine instructions, d i is the related deadline, and p i is the period with d i ≤ p i . In order to insure that a task is able to receive all data produced by its predecessors without any data being lost or duplicated [10], we assume that the successors' periods must be equal to or a multiple of those of the predecessors.

For any task τ i , its kth job is generated at every time unit r 0 i + kp i , and could be executed after the data from its predecessors has been received. We use J k i = r k i , c i , d k i to denote the kth job generated by τ i , where r k i , c i , and d i are the release time, computation workload and deadline time of J k i respectively.

div.p: III. SCHEDULABILITY ANALYSIS In this section, we analyze the constraints of periodic tasks with data dependency, and propose an exact formulation based on Linear Programming to determine the task schedulability.
When periodic tasks are schedulable on a heterogeneous multiprocessor platform, all tasks' jobs should meet constraints in space, time and precedence. Details are as follows:
1) Space constraint: (C1) Each job must be assigned to one and only one processor.

2) Time constraint: (C2) Each job should be executed after it is released and be finished before its deadline time. (C3) For jobs allocated to the same processor, overlap in execution times must be avoided.
3) Precedence constraint: (C4) Each job can start only after all data has been received from its predecessors.

Since each task generates a potentially infinite sequence of jobs, a schedulability interval is required for capturing the whole system behaviour. Schedulability interval is a finite time interval that the computation of a schedule during this interval provides enough information to determine the schedulability of a system [10]. If tasks' jobs are schedulable in the schedulability interval, it can be determined that all tasks are schedulable in this system. Goossens et al. [7] considered the periodicity of real-time schedules for dependent periodic tasks, and proposed a method to compute the schedulability interval on multiprocessor platforms. The schedulability interval is denoted by I, and can be calculated via,
div.formula: I = [0, H n i=1 (max(r 1 i + d i -p i , 0) + 1))
div.p: where H is the hyperperiod of the system and can be calculated via H = lcm(p 1 , ..., p n ).
We use g i and N I to denote the number of jobs that are generated by τ i and the number of jobs generated by all tasks during the schedulability interval I, i.e.,
div.formula: g i = H n i=1 (max(r 1 i + d i -p i , 0) + 1) p i N I = 1≤i≤n g i

div.head: D. Exact formulation
div.p: In this subsection, an exact formulation of the schedulability problem is proposed based on linear programming. We use the makespan (i.e., the maximum completion time of all jobs generated during the schedulability interval) as the objective function and try to minimize it as much as possible. Since J gi i is the last job generated by τ i , the makespan (denoted by M (I)) can be calculated via,
div.formula: M (I) = max 1≤i≤n (o i,gi + 1≤p≤m a i,gi,p ET i,p )
div.p: The schedulability problem is defined as minimizing a linear objective function (the makespan M (I) here) subject to linear constraints (the space, time and precedence constraints analyzed above). If the makespan obtained is not larger than the length of the schedulability interval, the heterogeneous multiprocessor system is schedulable. div.head: IV. LIST-BASED SCHEDULING ALGORITHM
div.p: In this section, we present a list-based scheduling algorithm to assign proper offsets and assignments for jobs generated by the periodic tasks. First a directed acyclic job graph is built to describe the dependency of jobs. Then, with this graph, a prioritizing phase is adopted to calculate the priorities of jobs. Finally, a processor selection phase is used to select the jobs in order of their priorities, and to assign the best processors to the selected jobs such that the jobs' finish time is minimized.

div.head: A. Directed acyclic job graph
div.p: We use a directed acyclic job graph D = (J, F ) to describe the dependency of jobs. J is the set of vertices representing the jobs and F is the set of directed edges indicating the dependency between jobs. As we pointed in Sect. div.p: Meanwhile, for two successive jobs generated by the same task, the first job must be executed before the second one. This precedence constraint can be regarded as a special data dependency constraint in which the amount of transferred data is zero, and can be expressed as:

div.head: B. Job prioritization
div.p: Job prioritization is an essential phase in list-based scheduling algorithms to compute the priorities of all jobs. In this work, inspired from HEFT upward rank proposed in [11], we use a modified upward rank (R u ) as the ranking function to compute the priorities and sort the jobs. The new ranking method is defined and recursively calculated as follows:
div.formula: Ru(J k i ) = ET (J k i )+ max J l j ∈Succ(J k i ) Ru(J l j )+max(r l j -d k i , T T (J k i , J l j ))(8)
div.p: where ET (J k i ) and T T (J k i , J l j ) are the average execution time of J k i and average communication time from J k i to J l j , respectively. The difference between our modified upward rank with the standard one is that our modified upward rank takes a job's deadline time and release time into consideration.

div.head: C. Processor selection
div.p: In our list-based scheduling algorithm, jobs are sorted by the non-increasing order of R u values. A job with high priority can be first chosen and assigned to the "best" processor, which guarantees that this job can have the minimum earliest finish time. An insertion-based policy is adopted that tries to insert a job in the earliest idle time slot between two already scheduled jobs on the same processor, if the idle time slot is large enough to execute the considered job.

EST (J k i , π q ) and EF T (J k i , π q ) are used to denote the earliest start time and the earliest finish time of job J k i on processor π q . Their values can be calculated recursively starting from the entry job after all of their immediate predecessor jobs have been scheduled:

div.p: where AF T (J l j ) is the actual finish time of J l j , T T (J l j , J k i ) is the data transfer time from J l j to J k i , ET (J k i , π q ) is the execution time of J k i on π q , and avail[π q ] is the earliest time at which the processor π q is ready to execute J l j . We use π best to denote the best processor selected by for the job J k i , then

( 9); V. CONCLUSIONS In this paper, we aimed at scheduling periodic tasks with data dependency on a heterogeneous multiprocessor platform. The tasks we considered generate jobs periodically and should be non-preemptively scheduled. We analyze the space, time and precedence constraints of tasks, and propose an exact formulation and a list-based scheduling algorithm to determine the schedulability of a system. The proposed approach helps in guiding the design of heterogeneous multiprocessor systems.
